title: dedicated-autoscaler-fleet-management-autoscaling-policies-and-util-reporting-enhancement
author: Avery Stone
release_notes: Improved dedicated fleet autoscaler policies to support per-priority throughput guarantees and burst token-bucket smoothing.
Exposed new utilization metrics (fleet_available_capacity, fleet_effective_burst_tokens) to the Console.
Default autoscaler policy tuned to reduce oscillations for short-lived burst traffic.
description:
Motivation: Customers running Dedicated fleets were seeing oscillations when short, high-concurrency bursts hit mixed-priority workloads. This caused unnecessary scale-ups and increased unit-costs. This PR implements a set of enhancements to the Dedicated autoscaler: (1) priority-aware throughput guarantees, (2) per-priority burst token-bucket smoothing and tunable burst budgets, and (3) improved fleet-level utilization reporting to make decisions and debugging easier.

Summary of changes: added a priority-aware token-bucket layer that isolates burst budgets per priority class and smooths short spikes; introduced new autoscaling policy parameters (min_guaranteed_rps_per_priority, burst_tokens_per_priority, smoothing_window_ms); surfaced two fleet-level metrics used by Console (fleet_available_capacity and fleet_effective_burst_tokens) and wired them into the fleet dashboard; updated default autoscaler tuning to prefer gradual scale-ups when bursts are detected and added a short-circuit fallback to best-effort routing under sustained pressure.

Compatibility: All defaults preserve current behavior for existing fleets. New parameters are optional and backward compatible. Existing Dedicated customers can opt-in by setting the new policy fields in their fleet config.

Testing: added unit tests for token-bucket math and priority accounting, integration tests that simulate mixed-priority workloads with bursty traffic, and end-to-end scenario validated on staging. CI pipeline runs build, unit, integration, and perf smoke tests.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc linked and reviewed (ENG-1482)
- [x] Unit tests
- [x] Integration tests
- [x] Console dashboard updates
- [x] Docs updated

References: Linear ENG-1482 (autoscaler design), ENG-1499 (observability), SUP-8273 (customer-reported oscillation incident).

Notes for reviewers: focus review on the token-bucket accounting (services/autoscaler/tokenbucket.go) and the interaction with the priority-aware routing table in services/routing. Performance sensitivity: the new smoothing window is configurable; default set to 5s to minimize additional CPU overhead while still smoothing most bursts.

review_comments: Priya Desai: Left a few nits on tokenbucket.go, primarily around integer math overflow in edge cases; suggest explicit int64 usage.
Avery Stone (author): Thanks, good catch — switched math to int64 and added bounds checks (see tokenbucket.go commit).
Jonah Kim: Integration tests look good. One question: can we expose burst_tokens_per_priority in API v1 for self-serve customers? Concerned about accidental misconfiguration.
Avery Stone: We decided to keep it opt-in for now; added docs and a warning in config validation. We can expose later after telemetry shows stable behavior.
Elena Morales: Can we add an alert when fleet_effective_burst_tokens falls below 10% of configured budget for more than 2 minutes?
Avery Stone: Added a Grafana alert rule draft in console/dashboards and created ENG-1499 to track alerting refinements.
summary_metrics_impact: Expected: 10-25% reduction in unnecessary scale-ups for mixed-priority burst traffic in staging tests.
notes: Staged rollout: enabled by default on staging fleets. Production rollout will be gradual and feature-flagged per fleet. Operations runbook updated under docs/dedicated/ops_autoscaler.md.
